newsitem.title: UK: Petrol bombs thrown at Northern Irish riot police.
newsitem.headline: Petrol bombs thrown at Northern Irish riot police.

text.p: Petrol bombs were hurled at Northern Ireland police as they broke up Protestant and Catholic rioters near the town of Lurgan in County Armagh, a police spokesman said on Wednesday.
Police fired eight plastic bullets when a dozen petrol bombs were thrown during the clashes, which flared on Tuesday night at a road separating rival housing areas.
Officers said they were attacked when they intervened to stop gangs throwing rocks and bottles.
Tension in the province has been high for many months because of renewed guerrilla conflict over the future of British rule.

Increased friction between pro-British Protestant and Irish Catholic hardliners has spilt over into a wave of retaliatory arson attacks on churches and community halls, street protests and sporadic rioting.
Four Catholic churches have been torched in the past two weeks and last weekend eight Catholic families fled an apartment block in Belfast which had been attacked by Protestant gang.
Security forces are on alert for attacks by Irish Republican Army guerrillas waging an escalating campaign against rule from London.
A ceasefire by Protestant guerrillas loyal to Britain is unstable, and "Loyalists" have been blamed for two killings and a spate of random vengeful attacks on Catholics in the past year.

Security sources fear more outbreaks of sectarian rioting in in sensitive flashpoint urban zones in the run up to a disputed series of summer marches by hardline Protestants. "It's heating up," said one officer.
